claim_text: Our I-GO Well initiative has made significant strides in supporting our people through musculoskeletal injury prevention and promoting psychosocial safety across our workplaces.
metric_name: training completion;Total recordable cases of work-related ill-health;
value_unit: %;Total recordable cases of work-related ill-health FY25;Total recordable cases of work-related ill-health FY24;%
context_text:
Of employees that were allocated the training on musculoskeletal injury prevention, 82% have completed the training. 
[table]Total recordable cases of work-related ill-health:
 4 (FY25) vs 26 (FY24); 
This year, the total number of recordable work-related ill health cases decreased by 85% with musculoskeletal disorders accounting for the majority of these ill health events.
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: The claim is supported because the report provides outcome-based evidence of a large reduction in recordable work-related ill health cases and also reports substantial completion of musculoskeletal injury prevention training.
llm_reason: The claim asserts 'significant strides' in musculoskeletal injury prevention and promoting psychosocial safety. The evidence shows 82% training completion for musculoskeletal injury prevention, which supports the training component. It also shows an 85% reduction in total recordable work-related ill-health cases (from 26 to 4), with musculoskeletal disorders as the majority, supporting injury prevention outcomes. However, the claim also mentions 'promoting psychosocial safety,' but the evidence only provides data on musculoskeletal disorders and total ill-health cases, with no specific evidence addressing psychosocial safety. Thus, the claim is partially supported for injury prevention but unsupported for psychosocial safety.
